reason: The cited evidence (E1) studies equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr alloys and the effect of removing individual elements, but it does not investigate partial substitution of Hf by Zr or compare densities; it provides no direct support for the key premises about density reduction or retained strength under the proposed non-equiatomic modification.
premises: Zr substitution for Hf preserves the disordered BCC solid-solution structure
Zr and Hf contribute similarly to solid-solution strengthening
Replacing Hf with Zr reduces density due to lower atomic weight of Zr
Mechanical properties (yield strength, ductility) remain nearly unchanged at room temperature and ~1000 °C
